Light day before the last week of the phase. Week 18 gave you numbers that are easy to compute and easy to misstate, so today is about the statements rather than the code.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State what VaR claims, what expected shortfall adds, and what both assume, from memory.
- Name the failure mode of each risk statistic you can compute.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>35 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Finish anything outstanding from days 120 to 125. The coverage and independence tests are the pieces to have working, since milestone 4 reports them.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Closed book: the precise claim of a 99 percent VaR, the subadditivity counterexample, the two backtest tests and what each catches, and the correlation conditioning argument. Say each out loud in under ninety seconds.
:::
:::

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, eighteenth sitting. Ten two-digit multiplications, the sevenths, and 1/3, 2/9 and 5/6 as decimals plus their reciprocals.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Poisson processes: buses arrive as a Poisson process with mean gap 10 minutes. You arrive at a random time. What is your expected wait, and what is the expected length of the gap you land in? Explain the inspection paradox out loud.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> The follow-up they use to check you understood: what is the expected time since the last bus? Give it without computing anything new.
:::
:::
